17:73.heading: Ayah 73

blocks.text: They were about to tempt you away from what We have revealed to you [O Prophet] so that you would fabricate something else and attribute it to Us; then they would have surely taken you as a close friend.

The verse identifies what lies at the heart of the confrontation: revelation itself. Opposition did not stop at rejecting the Quran or refusing to hear it; it extended to trying to influence its bearer so that something Allah had revealed would be changed, however slightly. This explains the recurring descriptions of the struggle over the Quran in this surah: “Indeed, this Qur’an guides to what is most upright”; “We have explained things in various ways in this Qur’an”; and “When you recite the Qur’an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter an invisible barrier[40].” Here the attempt reaches the point of seeking to have something other than what Allah revealed attributed to Him.

The attempt to turn the Messenger away from what was revealed to him therefore concerns the foundation of his mission, rather than a passing political disagreement.

17:74.heading: Ayah 74

blocks.text: Had We not made you stand firm, you would nearly have inclined to them a little.

Deliverance here is explicitly attributed to Allah’s making His Messenger firm. If the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), despite the completeness of his faith and knowledge, could not dispense with his Lord’s support, those serving the religion have still greater reason not to rely on their intelligence, understanding of circumstances or psychological strength. Knowing that an opponent intends to exploit you is not enough on its own.

17:75.heading: Ayah 75

blocks.text: In that case, We would have made you taste double punishment, both in this life and after death. Thereupon you would have found no helper against Us.

The warning is severe because revelation itself is at stake: the hypothetical consequence would be a doubled punishment in life and after death, with no protector against Allah. It corresponds to the warning against attributing to Allah words He did not say: “If he had falsely attributed something to Us, We would have surely seized him by the right hand[9], then severed his aorta[10], …” (Al-Haqqah: 44–46). Preserving the message takes precedence over its bearer’s comfort, reputation and gains.

But the explanation of that ruling must not be changed into something else to please people. The message is a coherent whole and must not be presented to people in a distorted form.

17:76.heading: Ayah 76

blocks.text: They were about to provoke you so as to drive you out of the land [of Makkah], but then they would not have remained after you, except for a little while[67].

After the attempt to divert through conciliatory pressure comes another: unsettling the Messenger so as to drive him out of the land. [The Arabic root behind «لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ» recurs in this surah in «وَاسْتَفْزِزْ», addressed to Satan, and «يَسْتَفِزَّهُمْ», describing Pharaoh’s intention. In this context, it conveys agitation that impels someone to act.] Satan is addressed with “Entice with your voice whoever of them you can”, the people of Makkah are described here, and Pharaoh later seeks to expel his opponents: “So he decided to exile them out of the land”. Such provocation is more than a calm removal. It drives someone into hurried, unsettled action by arousing fear, desire or anger, so that the decision comes at the moment the opponent chooses.

17:77.heading: Ayah 77

blocks.text: Such was Our way with the messengers We sent before you, and you will find no change in Our way.

The reference to Allah’s established way with earlier messengers places the situation within a recurring pattern in the history of revelation, rather than treating it as a personal crisis. Attempts to turn a messenger away from the truth are followed by pressure and offers, then by efforts to provoke and expel him. Intensifying pressure should not therefore be read as proof that the path is false or that Allah has abandoned those following it.

17:78.heading: Ayah 78

blocks.text: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night, and the recitation of dawn [prayer][68], for the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed [by the angels][69].

After describing the storms that seek to turn the heart away from revelation or push it into premature decisions, the surah gives a practical path to steadfastness: the prescribed prayers across the day and the Quran recited at dawn. Steadfastness is neither psychological toughness nor merely an understanding of hostile schemes. It is renewed connection with Allah throughout the day. The distribution of the prayers surrounds the day with worship, so that the heart is not left alone for long amid people’s clamor. Dawn is then singled out for Quran recitation. A person begins the day with the very words from which the defenders of falsehood seek to divert them, renewing their standard of judgment before entering a world of activity, pressure and negotiation.

17:79.heading: Ayah 79

blocks.text: And wake up during the night and pray, as an additional prayer for you [O Prophet], so your Lord may raise you to a praised status[70].

The command to rise at night with the Quran carries the means of steadfastness from the public activity of the day into the solitude of the night. [The Arabic «الهجود» originally means sleep, while «التهجد» carries the sense of casting sleep off and rising from it.] The body is not merely to remain awake; the heart, too, is to cast off heedlessness. An opponent may wait for a brief lapse through which bargaining, fear or haste can enter.

17:80.heading: Ayah 80

blocks.text: And say, “My Lord, make me enter an honorable entrance[71] and make me exit an honorable exit[72], and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority.”

After prayer and worship at night comes a supplication that guides every step: asking Allah for truthfulness in entering and leaving. Those defending falsehood may seek at one time to draw you into a settlement on their terms, and at another to provoke you into leaving on their timetable. Neither entering nor leaving should therefore follow personal desire, fear or the search for comfort. One enters because Allah requires it, and leaves when Allah permits it.

17:81.heading: Ayah 81

blocks.text: And say, “The truth has come and falsehood has perished. Indeed, falsehood is bound to perish[73].”

The arrival of truth and the passing of falsehood are proclaimed at a stage when outward victory was not yet complete. This shows that victory first takes shape when the bearer of truth preserves it: remaining faithful to revelation, refusing dependence on those seeking concessions and resisting provocation into a wrong course of action. When the bearer of the message stands firm, truth has prevailed in its first sphere; outward circumstances change afterward. Truth has strength in itself because it is revelation from Allah. Much of falsehood’s strength, by contrast, is borrowed from power, wealth, pressure and social standing, all of which can change. [The Arabic description «زَهُوقًا» conveys that falsehood is inherently liable to pass away.]

” (Al-Isra’: 82).

blocks.text: The remedy is not to dilute the Quran to make it acceptable to people, but to receive more of its guidance until the heart is healed of fear of them and their pressure. A clear example of one verse strengthening the community occurred when the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) died. Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) directed people back to Allah’s words: “Muhammad is no more than a messenger”, and revelation settled their hearts (Al-Bukhari: 4454).

blocks.text: Real renewal in people’s circumstances begins with a renewed reception of the Quran in their hearts. When that reception is sound, steadfastness is sound; when it weakens, a person becomes more vulnerable to temptation and provocation.
